name: NOVA Assistant
tag: One assistant console to chat, sort your day and run quick actions across the tools you already use.

scenarios.title: Sort a busy morning
scenarios.ask: I have {emails} unread emails and {meetings} meetings today. Sort what matters and draft what you can.
steps: Inbox reader
Read {emails} emails and grouped them: {=round(emails * 0.12)} need your reply, {=round(emails * 0.3)} are updates, the rest are newsletters and receipts.
Drafter
Wrote draft replies for {=round(emails * 0.08)} routine emails. They sit in your drafts folder for review.
Calendar agent
Prepared a one-line brief for each of your {meetings} meetings with the last email thread attached.
Task agent
Turned {=round(emails * 0.05)} requests into tasks with due dates.
followups: Does it send emails without asking?
No. Drafts wait for you. You can allow auto-send for specific cases later, such as meeting confirmations, but it is off by default.
Which tools does it connect to?
Email, calendar and a task list to start, plus quick actions for tools like your CRM or shared drive. You choose which ones it can see.
How did it decide what needs a reply?
It looks for direct questions, requests with dates and people you reply to often. You can correct it and it learns your pattern.

scenarios.title: Plan the week
scenarios.ask: I have {tasks} open tasks and about {hours} free hours this week. Plan it so the important work gets done.
steps: Task agent
Estimated time for each task. Total work is about {=round(tasks * 0.9)} hours.
Prioritizer
Ranked tasks by deadline and impact and marked {=ceil(tasks * 0.25)} as must-do.
Calendar agent
Blocked focus time for the must-do tasks in your quietest slots.
Planner
Suggested what to delegate or move to next week if it does not fit.
followups: What if a meeting lands on a focus block?
The assistant moves the block to the next open slot and tells you if that pushes a deadline.
It drafts the handoff message with context and a due date. You choose who gets it and press send.

scenarios.title: Follow up after a meeting
scenarios.ask: Turn my notes from a {mins} client meeting with {people} attendees into follow-ups.
steps: Notes reader
Read the notes and found {=max(2, round(mins / 10))} action items and {=max(1, round(mins / 30))} decisions.
Drafter
Wrote a recap email to all {people} attendees with decisions and owners.
Task agent
Created tasks for the {=max(1, round(max(2, round(mins / 10)) / 2))} items you own and added due dates.
Quick action
Logged the meeting on the client record in your CRM.
followups: Can it work from a recording?
Yes, if your meeting tool provides a transcript. The assistant reads the transcript the same way it reads notes.
What if it gets an owner wrong?
You edit the recap before it goes out. Corrections update the tasks too.
